findings.reason: a node implementing §7 as written would place new sessions on the engine being retired during the overlap window, the exact regression the cited code's own docstring says the rotation rule exists to prevent.
findings.text: §7's first placement rule ("the engine with the most free gate slots relative to its width") directs a new key to whichever engine is least loaded, so an idle draining width-4 engine (4/4 = 1.0) outranks a width-12 replacement carrying one request (11/12 = 0.92), while §7 says "an engine replacing a narrower one of the same model on the same server takes every new key, and the old engine drains" — the stated mechanism does not produce its own rotation clause, and it inverts the behaviour the existing `_preferred_owner` was written to keep ("Routing to the widest engine keeps that window free of a capacity regression", `imas_ambix/agent/router.py:1641`)

findings.reason: without a single writer for a multi-engine pool document the summed counts have no owner, so a node would either race two writers or invent the composition step the plan leaves unstated.
findings.text: §5 says "the router runs one publishing loop per engine and writes one document per pool at `lanes/<model id>.json`", but a pool with several engines (§7's case) then has two per-engine loops writing one path, and the section names no composer that owns the aggregated counts it specifies (running, waiting, ceilings, weighted per-request figures)

findings.reason: a node implementing §5 would change a schema version owned by another plan with no declared dependency telling it the owner changed the same document, which is how two plans come to disagree about one on-disk shape.
findings.text: §5 asserts it "bumps that schema's version" of "the versioned lane schema that local-lane-admission-control owns", and §4 binds every gate to that plan's `queue-order` decision, yet the plan's only declared relationship is `plan-after: local-lane-admission-control#s14` (a gate-width section)

findings.reason: a node dispatched for §11 has no red log showing that its own check can fail, which is the measure the review rubric and the node contract require of every implementable section.
findings.text: §11 declares four done-when bullets and no negative control, though it is an implementable section committed to a worker ("Any worker node can build them", §11 step 1)

findings.reason: the rollout check as written can never pass after §5 lands, so the operator would either record a false pass or discover the contradiction at deploy time.
findings.text: §11 step 2 records `lane.json` "from before and after the cycle: the same keys", but §5 has already added a top-level `lanes` index to `lane.json` and bumped the schema version, so the post-cycle document cannot have the same keys

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `topology.svg`, both research files (`serving-capacity-and-b300-projection`, `h200-b300-performance-comparison`), `local-lane-admission-control` (§s14 and the `queue-order` decision), `serving-record-warehouse`, `ops/lane-cycle/AGENTS.md` and `imas_ambix/agent/AGENTS.md` all resolve, and every cited symbol (`_publish_lane`, `_GenerationGate`, `_record_self_answer`, `_preferred_owner`, `newest_raw_receipt`, `SiteConfig`, `serve_grid`/`callers_table`/`serve_ledger_table`, `RECENT_TAIL_MAX_BYTES`, `reckon.crew.lane_document.read_lane_document`, `lane_callers.py`) exists at the base revision.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §11 ("Rollout, and who does each step") is an implementable section whose four done-when bullets name no negative control, and its step-2 measure ("the same keys") is falsified by §5's own added `lanes` key.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate in §3–§10 is a repo test run, whose log the run contract places on a durable path; §11's operator recordings name no path of their own, which the dispatch manifest supplies.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags reach a symbol or comment; `b300-role`, `watch-home` and `serving-figures-home` are decision keys, not code names.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's placement rule sends a new key to the engine with the most free slots relative to its width, which contradicts the section's own "the rotation case keeps today's behaviour" and would regress the replacement window the router's `_preferred_owner` protects; §5's "one publishing loop per engine writes one document per pool" names no single composer for a multi-engine pool document.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each implementable section (§3–§11) names one deliverable; §11 is the rollout of the others, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — `plan-after` names only `local-lane-admission-control#s14`, yet §5 states it bumps a lane schema that plan owns and §4 relies on that plan's `queue-order` decision, neither declared.
